assessment.summary: KRAS is one of the most extensively studied oncology targets, with exceptional structural coverage (556 PDB entries, best resolution 0.953Å), a large chemical dataset (5,903 IC50 entries), and two FDA-approved covalent inhibitors (sotorasib and adagrasib) targeting the G12C mutation. Druggability is high for the G12C mutant allele, though targeting other KRAS mutations (G12D, G12V, G12S, etc.) remains an active and partially unresolved challenge. Overall, KRAS represents a high-confidence, high-druggability target with strong disease validation across multiple cancers.
evidence_gaps: Approved drugs (sotorasib, adagrasib) are mutation-specific (G12C only); druggability of other KRAS mutants (G12D, G12V, G12S, Q61H, etc.) is less established with no approved drugs
Median IC50 of ~1020 nM suggests many chemical matter entries are of modest potency, indicating the broader chemical space beyond G12C inhibitors is still maturing
Resistance mechanisms (e.g., secondary KRAS mutations, bypass signalling via RTKs, MAPK reactivation) are not fully characterised and limit durable clinical benefit
Wild-type KRAS selectivity window: inhibitors must spare WT KRAS to avoid toxicity; therapeutic index data in normal tissues is incompletely defined
Pan-KRAS or allele-agnostic inhibitor strategies (e.g., SOS1 inhibitors, KRAS-PPI disruptors) are in early clinical stages with limited efficacy data
Combination therapy optimal partners and sequencing strategies remain under investigation
